children: Indonesia's cocoa grinding volume increased by 2% in the July-September quarter compared to the previous three-month period, the Indonesian Cocoa Association – Cocoa Sustainability Partnership (ASKINDO-CSP) said on Thursday.
The third-quarter cocoa grinding volume stood at 112,628 metric tons, the group said in a statement, up from 110,410 tons in the second quarter.
"This increase demonstrates the resilience of Indonesia's cocoa processing industry amid the current dynamics of the global cocoa market," said Jeffrey Haribowo, Chairman of ASKINDO-CSP.

Cocoa farmers have seen bean production in the peak harvest months of August to September drop by up to 15% compared to June because of drought, according to Arif Zamroni, chairman of Indonesian cocoa farmers group APKAI.
